name: Yangarra Estate Grenache High Sands 2016
text:
## Yangarra Estate Grenache High Sands 2016

**Australia's wine of the year.** This is the wine James Halliday named his 2020 Wine of the Year, the top award of the Halliday Wine Companion, with 99 points ([Fleurieu News](https://fleurieunews.com.au/NewsStory/hallidays-wine-of-the-year-goes-to-mclaren-vale-grenache/5d662414c31917002b07e059)). It was a rare honour for a [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), a grape that "doesn't get a lot of love from wine critics", as Anthony Gismondi put it ([Gismondi on Wine](https://gismondionwine.com/tasting-notes/201908/yangarra-high-sands-grenache-2016?note=30416)).

**The story.** Yangarra Estate is a single-vineyard estate in Blewitt Springs, at the northern edge of [McLaren Vale](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Yangarra+Estate+Vineyard,+McLaren+Flat+Road,+Kangarilla,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k). It began as the Eringa Park vineyard, bought in 2000 by California's [Jackson Family Wines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Family_Wines) and renamed ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Family_Wines)). Its 90-hectare vineyard is farmed organically and biodynamically, and its range is inspired by the southern Rhône ([McLaren Vale Grape Wine & Tourism Association](https://members.mclarenvale.info/news/media-releases/high-times-for-high-sands-grenache-as-halliday-crowns-2020-wine-of-the-year)).

**The winemaker.** Peter Fraser was Halliday's Winemaker of the Year in 2016; the 2015 High Sands had been Halliday's top wine in the "Other Red" category the year before. "Since my first vintage at Yangarra, the Grenache from this block has always shown remarkable character," he says. "We released the first vintage of High Sands in 2005" ([McLaren Vale association](https://members.mclarenvale.info/news/media-releases/high-times-for-high-sands-grenache-as-halliday-crowns-2020-wine-of-the-year)).

**The wine: High Sands.** High Sands comes from a 1.7-hectare block at the highest point of the estate: dry-grown bush vines planted in 1946 in white sands said to be over 50 million years old ([McLaren Vale association](https://members.mclarenvale.info/news/media-releases/high-times-for-high-sands-grenache-as-halliday-crowns-2020-wine-of-the-year)). Gismondi adds that it is Block 31, at 210 metres, with the deepest sand and the lowest vigour and yield. The fruit is hand-picked, wild-fermented and aged 11 months in older French oak, then bottled unfined and lightly filtered ([Gismondi on Wine](https://gismondionwine.com/tasting-notes/201908/yangarra-high-sands-grenache-2016?note=30416)). The Yangarra team calls it "our grail" ([Fleurieu News](https://fleurieunews.com.au/NewsStory/hallidays-wine-of-the-year-goes-to-mclaren-vale-grenache/5d662414c31917002b07e059)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) says 2016 was another very early vintage, with most regions finished by mid-February; a warm summer gave full flavour ripeness. It was "a compressed and difficult vintage", but the results promised well.

**What the critics say for 2016.**
- **[James Halliday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Halliday_%28writer%29): 99**, and his 2020 Wine of the Year ([Fleurieu News](https://fleurieunews.com.au/NewsStory/hallidays-wine-of-the-year-goes-to-mclaren-vale-grenache/5d662414c31917002b07e059)).
- **Anthony Gismondi, Gismondi on Wine: 96** (August 2019, [review](https://gismondionwine.com/tasting-notes/201908/yangarra-high-sands-grenache-2016?note=30416)). "Aromatic, creamy, classic, pure red fruit flavours with vibrant, smooth textures". It is 14.5% alcohol, "but you feel none of it amid the savoury mix of minerals and fruit", and the oak is "not noticeable". "This one should change a few minds about the real potential of this grape variety. Brava Mr. Fraser."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.3** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2022 to 2031. So it is in its prime: perfumed red fruit, spice and sandy, savoury minerality. Serve it slightly cool, at about 15 to 16°C, and decant it for about an hour.

**Food.** Roast lamb with garlic and rosemary, duck with cherries, or a mushroom risotto.

**Value and where to buy.** High Sands sold out at the cellar door in 2019, when it cost $150 a bottle there ([Fleurieu News](https://fleurieunews.com.au/NewsStory/hallidays-wine-of-the-year-goes-to-mclaren-vale-grenache/5d662414c31917002b07e059)), and it rarely reaches stores. Yangarra's other wines are easy to find: BSW Liquor has the Old Vine Grenache 2023 and the GSM at $42.99, and ZYN has the McLaren Vale Grenache 2022 at $37.80.

**From the history books**
- **Named for a McLaren.** McLaren Vale was named after either David McLaren, Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company, or John McLaren, who surveyed the area in 1839. The first settlers grew cereal crops, but John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines in 1838, and the forerunners of today's Seaview and Hardys wineries were running by 1850 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Century-old vines.** Some McLaren Vale vines more than 100 years old are still producing ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)), and the region is a member of the Great Wine Capitals of the World network.
- **Between the gulf and the hills.** The region runs 30 km down the coast of the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) to the foothills of the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges), with a [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate) of four clear seasons ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Penfolds comes south.** Between 1904 and 1912 [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), then the largest winery around Adelaide, bought vineyards in McLaren Vale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

**Curious details**
- **A rare grape in the Vale.** Only 6.15% of McLaren Vale's vineyard is Grenache, yet the region's Grenache history goes back to the 1800s ([McLaren Vale association](https://members.mclarenvale.info/news/media-releases/high-times-for-high-sands-grenache-as-halliday-crowns-2020-wine-of-the-year)).
- **Restaurant tip.** When the award was announced and the winery sold out, Yangarra's brand manager tipped two local restaurants, the Salopian Inn and the Victory Hotel, as the last places with a few bottles ([Fleurieu News](https://fleurieunews.com.au/NewsStory/hallidays-wine-of-the-year-goes-to-mclaren-vale-grenache/5d662414c31917002b07e059)).
